comparator.name: Biology
comparator.sourceNotes: UvA Biology builds a foundation across molecules, cells, organisms and ecosystems. Lab work, fieldwork and quantitative methods prepare students to design and carry out research. In year three, students have 30 EC of elective space and complete a required 18 EC bachelor project.
components: Cellular and molecular biology with laboratory work.
Learn to collect research data and use statistics and R to analyse it.
Includes field research and practical work.
Ziekte en afweer van plant en dier
Write a literature review in English on a current biology topic.
Includes DNA and biochemical laboratory techniques.
Research Project Challenges in Ecology and Evolution
Team field and/or laboratory research with scientific reporting.
Choose biology electives, a minor, study abroad or other approved electives.
Design and carry out an individual biology research project, present the results and write a scientific report.

alternatives.label: Biological sciences
alternatives.labelReason: The official programme spans life from molecules and cells through organisms, biodiversity and ecosystems, supported by laboratory, field, statistical and computational methods.
alternatives.concept: Study life from cells and genes to organisms and ecosystems. Build from biodiversity and molecular biology to genetics, laboratory work, marine ecology and the effects of farming on biodiversity.
progression: The life sciences foundation comes before molecular cell biology, biochemistry and lab work. Early biodiversity and ecosystem study supports marine biology and sustainable farming. Mathematics precedes statistics.

alternatives.label: Molecular biology, health and biological data
alternatives.labelReason: The comparator teaches molecular biology, immunity and quantitative research, and allows further study in biomedical and molecular life sciences.
alternatives.concept: Explore how cells work and how biological processes contribute to health and disease. Study biochemistry, infection and genetics, then use statistics, epidemiology and computing to investigate biological and health data.
progression: Life sciences and brain foundations precede advanced work in genetics, disease and neuroscience. Programming, data science and mathematics precede machine learning and deep learning.
alternatives.distinctness: This option differs from Biological sciences by 60 EC each way. It gives more space to neuroscience, epidemiology and computational methods.

alternatives.label: Ecology, evolution and conservation
alternatives.labelReason: The official programme explicitly develops evolution, ecology, biodiversity, field research, marine and freshwater biology, environmental change and conservation-related applications.
alternatives.concept: Study how organisms evolve, interact and respond to environmental change. Use marine biology, soil and water science, biogeochemistry and pollution remediation to explore what shapes habitats and biodiversity.
progression: Start with life sciences, biodiversity and sustainability. Build toward evolution, ecosystems, conservation and the study of soils and water. Sustainability Essentials II precedes remediation.
alternatives.distinctness: This option differs from Biological sciences by 60 EC and from Molecular biology, health and biological data by 120 EC each way. It focuses on the environment, biodiversity and conservation.

core: Living organisms and biological systems from molecules to ecosystems
Genes, genomes, cells, biomolecules and molecular mechanisms
Plants, animals, microorganisms, physiology and organismal biology
Biological modelling, statistics, bioinformatics and quantitative evidence
Experimental, laboratory, field and independent biological research
adjacent: Health, biomedical research, biotechnology and toxicology
Human impacts, environmental change and nature conservation
Neurobiology and biological bases of behaviour
questions: How do biological systems function from molecules and cells to organisms and ecosystems?
How do evolution and human activity shape biodiversity, ecosystems and conservation needs?
How can molecular, computational and experimental biology address health and sustainability challenges?

candidates.label: Molecular biology, health and biological data
Neurobiology and evolutionary psychobiology
candidates.reason: Neurobiology and evolutionary psychobiology have a real elective basis. UCR covers comparative neurobiology, perception and brain functions, but the specialist evolutionary behaviour sequence is thinner. The three retained options cover more of the Biology target.

trace: Builds academic writing, literature synthesis and research-question skills.
Introduces biomolecules, cell structures, energy metabolism, cellular communication, DNA and heredity.
Surveys the tree of life, microorganisms, plants, animals and methods for investigating biodiversity.
Builds Python programming and computational problem-solving.
Develops molecular-cell biology, genomes, gene expression, signalling, division, tissues and current research methods.
Examines extinction, human impacts and scientific and policy responses in conservation biology.
Covers ecological processes from organisms to ecosystems and introduces ecological modelling.
Provides mathematical techniques needed for quantitative and computational biological work.
Examines molecules, cells, tissues, organ systems, homeostasis and organismal physiology.
Covers biomolecules, metabolism, signalling and biochemical foundations of biotechnology and disease.
Studies evolutionary mechanisms from genes to populations and their application across biology.
Adds probability, distributions, sampling, estimation and simulation for biological inference.
Provides molecular and microbiological laboratory work, including proteins, PCR, electrophoresis and bioinformatics.
Studies microbes, host–pathogen interaction, innate and adaptive immunity and immunopathology.
Provides comparative neurobiology, animal behaviour, microscopy, anatomy and experimental ethics.
Connects organisms and ecosystems to soil processes, water and environmental conditions.
Advances molecular genetics, mutation, inheritance, pathology, testing and treatment.
Applies molecular, cellular and physiological regulation to pharmacology and toxic effects.
Examines marine ecosystem processes, from coastal and estuarine systems to reefs and the deep sea, and pressures including plastic pollution.
Introduces data preparation, analysis, visualisation and evidence-based computational inquiry.
Relates embryology, anatomy and physiology to mechanisms of disease across organ systems.
Develops structure–function reasoning through human anatomy, imaging and anatomical variation.
Examines geoscience hazards, climate risks and adaptation as context for environmental change.
Adds governance, interests, public evidence and implementation for environmental and conservation action.
Introduces neurons, brain organisation, behaviour and neuroscience research methods.
Develops neural-network methods for classification, images and time series.
Examines neural mechanisms of perception and goal-directed action through cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology.
Extends biological and cognitive analysis to advanced brain functions.
Introduces predictive modelling and machine-learning workflows for complex data.
Develops image analysis, feature detection and tracking, with applications including medicine.
Introduces environmental systems, sustainability problems and interdisciplinary analysis.
Applies physical concepts and measurement techniques to sustainability, including waves, spectroscopy and microscopy.
Provides Earth-system context for habitats, climate and long-term environmental change.
Examines climate processes, evidence, impacts and responses shaping biological systems.
Examines agricultural and horticultural systems and their effects on wildlife, biodiversity and the environment.
Connects biological systems to nutrient cycles and chemical processes in the environment.
Uses system modelling and proxy data to investigate interactions among Earth systems.
Develops numerical approximation, error and stability analysis, including differential equations relevant to biological models.
Adds applied pollution and soil remediation, including plant- and fungus-based methods, within a wider resource recovery course.
Uses epidemiological study designs, incidence, prevalence and confounding to examine health evidence.
blocks: Biological foundations: cells, organisms and diversity
Both introduce cells, biomolecules and molecular processes. UvA also requires practical work in cellular and molecular techniques.
UvA develops writing and presentation skills specifically for biology. UCR teaches academic writing in Personal & Professional Development.
UvA studies genetic mechanisms and evolutionary change together in the first year.
UvA surveys bacteria, fungi, protists and viruses. UCR covers parts of this material in biodiversity, lab and infection courses.
Both teach animal structure and function. UCR concentrates on human physiology.
UvA requires a dedicated course in plant structure, reproduction and stress responses.
UvA students analyse a sustainability problem and write policy advice in teams.
Both study biodiversity and organism identification. UvA also has a dedicated ecology field investigation.
UvA reserves 30 EC in year three for electives.
Molecular, cellular, physiological and biomedical biology
Both study how molecular mechanisms regulate cell function, including gene expression and signalling.
Both study nervous systems and behaviour. UCR includes comparative anatomy, animal behaviour and welfare.
Both investigate pathogens and immune defences. UCR focuses on human immunity, while UvA also studies plant defences.
Both use DNA and biochemical laboratory techniques. UvA also applies these techniques to food, health and sustainability questions.
UvA students design and carry out an ecology or evolution study in teams and write a scientific report.
Evolution, ecology, conservation and environmental systems
Both use population dynamics to investigate biological interactions. UvA applies these models to problems such as fisheries and pest control.
Both study evolutionary genetics, ecology and phylogeny.
Quantitative methods, research and open study space
UvA uses quantitative methods to investigate biological causes. UCR provides general training in probability and statistical inference.
UvA introduces bioinformatics in a required biology project. UCR builds general computing and data analysis skills.
UvA requires an 18 EC project. The 15 EC optional UCR research element sits outside the illustrated schedules.

selection.assessment: The broad option retains a cells-to-ecosystems spine. The two other options build sustained emphases around molecular and health science with quantitative methods, and around ecology and environmental change. Comparative neurobiology contributes to the broad and molecular options. A separate behaviour option would cover less of the Biology target.

notes.text: UvA requires dedicated plant and animal biology courses, team research in the field or lab, and an 18 EC individual project. The UCR options combine relevant courses in different ways. They cover parts of the same biology and research methods, with less dedicated study of plants and nonhuman animal physiology.

audience.programmeDescription: UvA Biology studies life from cells to ecosystems through experiments, fieldwork and data analysis. The third year combines elective study with an individual research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers three ways to study related questions. One spans biological scales, one focuses on molecular biology and health, and one emphasises ecology and conservation.
